Skills are such a good idea.
Skills are here to stay. The Skills spec[] is clever, progressive disclosure is really what was needed.
Skills are to the LLM what packages are to your programming language of choice (unless you're writing C apparently)

Skills factorise common operations you like into a shorter interface. It's a good-enough attempt at providing more reproducibility to LLM outputs.
Skills are supported by most of the tools out there : OpenCode, Mistral Vibe, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI ...

Currently, skills can be located in your global folder (say, ~/.claude/skills or ~/.agents/skills), or in your local repo.
Some tools like Claude Code support an --add-dir argument to specify another folder to add to the session, and if this folder contains skills they are added to the context.

Current issues :
- Growing libraries of skills. They will grow naturally. We all like to hoard : install <pkg> just to test and then forget about your global machine library. But current solutions like npx skills Vercel add the skills either to global or local. No "unactivated" skills anywhere.
- Skills going stale : npx skills does that well. I don't know if it tracks in-repo skills well but at least it updates global skills, I've tried it.
- Skills distribution : if you are testing many CLI tools (they change all the time), you need skills in .claude, .agents, .vibe ...
- Git pollution : your global skills influence the LLM output but you're not committing them to the repo. Why would you want to commit some inside the repo ? You want skills that operate at the repo level, because your R skills are useless in your Rust crate, but they are here to affect the LLM behavior. I understand and share the need to tell others that LLMs are working on this repo and which skills they are using, but do you need to share the full text ? It's not really a good fit amongst the commits that change / fix and otherwise progress your project

Solutions :

- A cold storage : a central source of truth, a place where you can access skills you need at any time, but not activated (in context for the LLM). Managed by a program, with metadata to power skills search, discovery, update, adding and removing, and publishing (you can make skills faster than packages !)
- A declarative file for skills dependencies : like packages, we can have a file that tells others what we use, maybe even which revision.
- Using a staging fleeting folder : when you run claude() or vibe(), add a folder that reads the skills-deps file and adds the skills to that folder. Not seen by git, but in context for the llm.
- Commands to update your skills, like with packages.

Where I am now : rplsmn/shared-safe-config (rename !)

I have :

- A machine setup script that installs Claude Code, Open Code, Mistral Vibe, Copilot CLI and wrappers around their entrypoints add start and stop hooks.
  - on startup, 2 directories are added : 1) the ARTIFACTS_DIR where agents store their ... artifacts ! That means plans, specs, reserach reports etc and 2) a temporary (lifetime = session) dir where local skills are symlinked depending on a manifest file in the repo
  - on exit, the artifact dir makes a commit, and pushes to the remote, the temp-dir is destroyed.
- A registry that saves skills and agents to a central location and serves symlinks to the relevant folders for all 4 tools
- A script to automate the distribution of global scripts via a library.json file where core:true means the skill goes to global, and the rest is cold
- A bash tool that can :
  - Add / remove a local skill to a repo via a symlink ; tracked only by a manifest file in the repo
  - List skills available on the machine, and their activation state
  - Add / remove *temporary* skills to the temporary session dir (without editing the manifest)
  - Synchronise the global library when the registry changes
  - Promote a skill to the registry when it's mature

I want to add :

- Adding a skill found in the while, starting with github repo
- Managing skills versions, and their origin, for update / retrograde from the cli
- Declaring skill dependencies on each other
- A proper search interface + function for finding skills in a repo + and auto add based on patterns in the repo (R markers, cargo.toml, env descriptions ...)
- Extract the management of my gitconfig to another tool !!
